subject: Tool calling integration post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finapps.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@finapps.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Tool calling patterns, auth, and next steps

Thanks again for the call today — really useful session. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration approach and risks.

Summary of what we covered:
- Goals: allow FinApps to call a mix of internal services (accounting lookup, transaction enrichment) and 3rd-party data providers via a unified tool/call interface from the Redwood runtime.
- Key features you want: explicit tool definitions, typed/structured outputs for downstream handlers, parallel tool execution for enrichment, safe retries and idempotency, and seamless auth delegation for customer-owned APIs.
- Constraints: low tail latency (<250ms P50 for enrichment calls), strict data residency for some workflows, and SOC 2 / auditability requirements.

Proposed integration pattern (high-level):
1) SDK setup: use Redwood SDK client in your backend to make model calls + tool execution. We recommend the lightweight SDK (node/python) with persistent connection (HTTP/GRPC) for lower latency. See attached redwood-sdk-setup.md.
2) Tool definitions: define tools as named endpoints with an explicit JSON schema for inputs/outputs. Example YAML attached (sample-tool-defs.yaml).
3) Routing & auth: tools can be routed by policy (region, cost tier). For customer-owned services, we recommend token-exchange: FinApps provides short-lived service account tokens to Redwood via their KMS or the token exchange flow described in the doc.
4) Parallel tools & orchestration: for enrichment, run tools in parallel and aggregate results in a structured response (reranker/embeddings step optional).
5) Error handling & fallbacks: canonical error categories (transient, permanent, partial-data). Redwood can retry transient errors (exponential backoff) and return partial results with error metadata for downstream logic.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm the list of services you want exposed as tools and whether they require customer-managed credentials? (Priya: can you share the service inventory CSV)
- Schedule a 90-minute architecture workshop with your infra team + our engineering (Dev) to go over auth and routing (proposed: Tue 4/13 or Thu 4/15).
- We'll prepare a starter set of tool defs and an example parallel-execution pattern using embeddings + reranker for the enrichment use case.

Attaching: integration diagram, sample tool defs, SDK setup doc.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Tool calling patterns, auth, and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and lines up with our internal thinking. Quick answers:
- Service inventory: Priya is looping in the owner list; we'll share the CSV by EOD Monday (4/12).
- Customer-managed creds: our payments enrichment service will need to remain behind our VPC and requires short-lived credentials; other public data providers can use a Redwood-managed service account.
- Workshop: Thu 4/15 10:00am PT works for us. Could you send a calendar invite for 90 minutes and include an agenda?

A couple of technical clarifications for Dev:
- For parallel enrichment, latency sensitivity is high; can Redwood provide a per-request deadline so we can cancel slower secondary tool calls?
- For structured output, we prefer a JSON-LD-ish schema so we can map fields into our pipelines.

Alex
VP Product, FinApps
alex.torres@finapps.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finapps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Tool calling patterns, auth, and next steps

Alex — great questions. Quick technical notes ahead of the workshop:
- Per-request deadlines: yes — the SDK exposes a per-call timeout and we also support cancellation tokens (HTTP/GRPC). Redwood will enforce a soft deadline at the runtime layer and can cancel outstanding tool RPCs when the deadline expires. We'll include example code in the workshop.
- Structured output: JSON Schema works well; we can also publish example JSON-LD mappings. Our tool-definition format in the sample YAML supports an output schema field and verification hooks.

Error handling policy (summary):
- Transient errors: automatic retries (configurable up to N attempts) with jittered backoff. For parallel executions we retry only idempotent calls or those marked safe_to_retry.
- Partial failures: runtime will return available tool outputs plus an errors array with structured error_type and tool_id so your app can decide to degrade gracefully.
- Permanent failures: surface as structured error and don't retry.

I'll prepare a short tech checklist and a sample tool-def set that demonstrates:
- tool calling with auth header exchange
- parallel enrichment pattern (Promise.all style with deadline enforcement)
- embeddings + reranker step for selecting best enrichment result

See attached sample-tool-defs.yaml; I'll bring a live demo to the architecture workshop.

—Dev

- vendor-lookup (owner: L. Gomez) — public HTTPS, rate limits need consideration

Other asks:
- Security/compliance: can Redwood provide audit logs for tool invocations (who/when/inputs masked)? We need this for SOC 2.
- Data retention: for PII enrichment flows, we need optional opt-out so data isn't persisted in any cache.
